title.narrative: Provision of integrated agriculture and protection services for improved food security in El fasher and Al lait North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International and its partner Auttach for Peace and Development (APD) aim to address acute food insecurity in North Darfur, particularly in the El Fasher-Zamzam IDP camp, classified as IPC Phase 5 (famine) in August 2024. The famine is expected to persist and expand to areas like Al Lait through May 2025. Key protection risks include risk of GBV during agricultural activities and aid distribution, exclusion of marginalized groups from assistance, and conflict over scarce resources like arable land between farmers and nomads. Additionally, displacements disrupting livelihoods and negative coping mechanisms, such as child labor and marriage, endanger children. Poorly managed distribution points and unsafe transit routes further expose vulnerable groups to sexual exploitation and violence. This project will support 17,390 individuals by enhancing food production and strengthening livelihoods. RI will distribute improved varieties of crop and vegetable seeds, and agricultural toolkits, with complementary training on climate smart , good agricultural practices (GAPs) with focus on nutrition sensitive agriculture, and income-generating activities (IGAs)like food processing, tailoring and other activities inform by market assessments, community needs, and local cultural practices to ensure relevance, sustainability, and alignment with available market opportunities. ltbrgt RI proposes a Protection and Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) integrated project, with an inclusive approach to benefit all. RI to engage the crop protection committees (CPCs), community-based protection networks (CBPNs), and reconciliation committees to protect livelihoods and address risks of theft, local disputes, and conflicts over land and resources. These committees will engage the stakeholders through dialogue, reduce tensions, and promote social cohesion. CBPNs will address local protection concerns, ensuring equitable access to resources for marginalized groups. All activities will follow a conflict-sensitive approach, guided by the "do no harm" principle. RI will conduct risk assessment, conflict analyses, engage communities, and ensure transparent beneficiary selection. In addition to FSL activities, RI’s Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ESNFI) response aligns with the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), specifically Strategic Objective One (SO1), which seeks to provide gender-responsive life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable. RI will distribute essential ESNFI kits to 440 households in North Darfur, including tarpaulins, blankets, sleeping mats, cooking utensils, solar lamps, and jerry cans. These items will address immediate shelter and non-food needs, improving living conditions and reducing exposure to harsh environmental conditions. ltbrgtThe Theory of Change: If RI and partners implement integrated food security, NFIs and protection interventions and if communities are equipped with training, awareness and capacities then improved food security, reduced protection risks, and enhanced resilience to ongoing shocks is enhanced fostering long-term community cohesion and stability. ltbrgtThe response will target the vulnerable groups, including displaced individuals, host communities, women and girls with high protection risks, individuals with disabilities, elderly, and GBV survivors. Targeting and verification will follow FSL and Protection cluster guidelines/SOPs, and criteria contextualized.nbsp ltbrgtRI will ensure accountability through rigorous ME, adaptive programming, transparent and inclusive targeting mechanisms, entitlement notifications, and beneficiary feedback systems. Post-distribution monitoring and satisfaction surveys will assess effectiveness and gather insights for improvement. By addressing both food insecurity and emergency shelter needs, this integrated response will enhance the resilience and well-being of the most vulnerable populations in North Darfur and ensure interventions remain relevant and effective. ltbrgtlt/pgt
